context:
Build the workflow changes incrementally:
  1. cancel-in-progress (w1) is a small, low-risk YAML edit
  2. Auto-revert (w2) is the substantive change — use peter-evans/
     create-pull-request@v6 (mature, well-tested) rather than rolling
     a custom revert script
  3. Metrics (w3) is independent of auto-revert; both can run in
     parallel jobs in the same workflow
  4. Make target (w5) is the human-facing surface for w3
  5. Docs (w4) once the behavior is confirmed
  6. Smoke test in fork (w6) BEFORE merging — auto-revert that
     opens spurious PRs would be very noisy to roll back

For revert conflicts: the fallback to "open an issue" is intentional.
An auto-revert that conflicts probably means later commits depend on
the broken one, so a human needs to decide whether to revert the
whole stack or fix forward.

For metrics: keep it simple. JSON files in workflow artifacts, no
database, no service. Step 5 reads the last 30 days and aggregates.
If we end up wanting longer retention, push to a `metrics` orphan
branch instead — but that's a Step 5 decision, not Step 4.
description:
Strengthens `develop-post-merge.yml` so that relaxing strict-base in
Step 3 has a credible safety net, not just a notification. When
develop goes red post-merge, the workflow automatically opens a revert
PR for the offending SHA (or an issue if revert conflicts), and emits
basic dev-loop metrics that feed Step 5's measurement window.

Sequence: this MUST land after Step 3 (relaxed strict-base), because
the auto-revert is the mitigation for the increased post-merge risk
introduced by Step 3.

Single PR via `make pr-open`.

work_units.notes:
Currently the workflow likely has a `concurrency:` block that
may cancel in-progress runs when a new push lands. Change:
  concurrency:
    group: develop-post-merge-${{ github.sha }}
    cancel-in-progress: false
Group key on `github.sha` (not `github.ref`) so each landed SHA
gets its own concurrency lane and runs to completion. This is
necessary so fast-landing PRs don't cause the workflow to skip
checking intermediate SHAs.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Updated `.github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml` so the
    concurrency group is `develop-post-merge-${{ github.sha }}`.
  - Set `cancel-in-progress: false` so a later push to `develop`
    cannot cancel the post-merge safety check for an earlier landed SHA.

New job `auto-revert-on-failure` triggered by
`workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure'` (or as a continuation
job in the same workflow with `if: failure()`). Steps:
  1. Identify the failing SHA (`github.sha` of the post-merge run)
  2. Identify the PR that introduced the SHA via
     `gh pr list --state merged --search "<sha>"`
  3. Create branch `auto-revert/<short-sha>` from develop
  4. `git revert --no-edit <sha>` (single SHA, no merge commits)
  5. If revert succeeds: push branch, open PR with title
     `Revert <pr-title> (#<pr-num>) — develop went red post-merge`,
     body includes failing run URL + originating PR link, label
     `incident:develop-red`, request review from PR author
  6. If revert fails (conflict): open issue with same metadata,
     label `incident:develop-red-revert-conflict`, no PR
Use `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6` action or a small
gh-cli script.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Added `auto-revert-on-failure` to
    `.github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml` with
    `needs: [lint, fast-test]` and an `always()` guard that runs only
    when one of those post-merge checks fails.
  - Added job-level permissions `contents: write`,
    `pull-requests: write`, and `issues: write`, which are the minimum
    scopes needed to push a revert branch and open either a PR or issue.
  - Used an inline `gh` script so the same job can identify the
    associated squash-merge PR, create idempotent incident labels, open
    an `auto-revert/<short-sha>` PR when `git revert --no-edit` succeeds,
    and request review from the originating PR author when possible.
  - Added conflict fallback: if the revert does not apply cleanly, the
    job aborts the revert and opens an
    `incident:develop-red-revert-conflict` issue with the failing SHA,
    run URL, originating PR URL, and attempted branch name.
  - W2 review issue addressed during implementation: the job uses
    `needs.*.result` rather than job-level `failure()` alone, so skipped
    or successful post-merge jobs do not accidentally trigger a revert.
work_units.summary: Add auto-revert PR generation on red

work_units.notes:
Add a `metrics` job that runs with `if: always()` for every push to
develop, so both green and red post-merge runs emit a machine-readable
record. Computes and writes JSON artifact:
  {
    "merged_at": "<ISO-8601>",
    "pr_number": N,
    "pr_open_to_merged_seconds": N,
    "post_merge_red": false,
    "develop_red_detected_at": null,
    "auto_revert_pr_opened_at": null,
    "time_to_revert_pr_seconds": null,
    "next_green_develop_run_at": null,
    "time_to_recover_red_seconds": null,
    "conflict_on_merge": <bool from PR labels/comments>,
    "orphaned_failed_pr": false,
    "ci_runner_minutes": N
  }
On failure, the auto-revert job should update or emit the same shape
with `post_merge_red: true`, `develop_red_detected_at`, and
`auto_revert_pr_opened_at`. `next_green_develop_run_at` and
`time_to_recover_red_seconds` may be null at artifact creation time;
`make dev-loop-metrics` must fill them by scanning later successful
develop-post-merge runs. Artifact retention: 90 days (covers the
Step 5 measurement window). One file per merge. Step 5 aggregates
these records plus the explicit PR audit sources named there.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Added a `metrics` job to `.github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml`
    with `if: always()` and `needs: [lint, fast-test,
    auto-revert-on-failure]`, so every develop push emits metrics after
    the selected post-merge checks and any auto-revert attempt finish.
  - The metrics job uses read-only `actions`/`contents` permissions,
    queries the associated squash-merge PR through GraphQL, and writes
    `dev-loop-metrics/<sha>.json`.
  - The JSON includes the Step 4 shape: merge timestamp, PR number,
    PR-open-to-merge seconds, post-merge red status, red detection time,
    auto-revert PR timestamp when one was opened, recovery placeholders,
    conflict/orphan flags, and summed completed-job runner minutes.
  - Added a 90-day artifact upload named `metrics` for Step 5's
    measurement window.
  - W3 review issue addressed during implementation: the metrics job
    has only read permissions, and the GitHub jobs query requests one
    bounded page (`per_page=100`) so the captured payload is valid JSON.
  - W3 review timing issue fixed: `develop_red_detected_at` is derived
    from the failed `lint`/`fast-test` job completion timestamp instead
    of the later metrics-job start time, so `time_to_revert_pr_seconds`
    cannot go negative when auto-revert finishes before metrics runs.
work_units.summary: Emit per-PR dev-loop metrics as workflow artifact

work_units.notes:
Add a section "If develop goes red":
  - The post-merge workflow detects the failure within ~5 min
  - It auto-opens a revert PR (label: incident:develop-red) OR
    an issue if revert conflicts
  - Original PR author gets review-requested on the revert
  - Agents do NOT need to monitor CI proactively
  - To repair: `make worktree-claim BRANCH=fix/<original-issue>`,
    fix, resubmit
Replace any older "monitor your PR until green" guidance.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Updated `CLAUDE.md` with an "If develop goes red" flow: the
    post-merge workflow opens an `incident:develop-red` revert PR, or an
    `incident:develop-red-revert-conflict` issue when the revert
    conflicts.
  - Updated `AGENTS.md` with the same operating guidance and removed
    the placeholder language that Step 4 would expand the safety net
    later.
  - Documented that agents do not need to monitor CI proactively after
    auto-merge; the generated revert PR or conflict issue is the alert.
  - Documented the repair path:
    `make worktree-claim BRANCH=fix/<original-issue>`, fix, preflight,
    and resubmit with `make pr-open`.
work_units.summary: Document the new failure flow in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md

work_units.notes:
`make dev-loop-metrics` downloads the last N (default 30) days
of metrics artifacts and prints a summary:
  - P50/P95 PR-to-merged time
  - Post-merge red rate
  - Conflict rate
  - Runner minutes total
Used by Step 5 reviewer (manual or scripted) to check thresholds.
Implementation: `gh run list --workflow develop-post-merge.yml
--json conclusion,databaseId | gh run download <id> -n metrics`,
then aggregate the JSON files.
Document this target in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md near the post-merge
safety-net / dev-loop workflow text. In CLAUDE.md, add it to the
pre-approved read-only PR/Worktree or metrics bucket; the command
reads workflow artifacts through `gh` and does not mutate repo state.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - Added `make dev-loop-metrics` with `DEV_LOOP_METRICS_DAYS` (default
    30) and `DEV_LOOP_METRICS_LIMIT` (default 100). The target lists
    recent `develop-post-merge.yml` push runs on `develop`, downloads
    available `metrics` artifacts, and aggregates their JSON files.
  - The summary prints metrics artifact count, P50/P95 PR-to-merged
    seconds, post-merge red rate, conflict rate, and total runner
    minutes. If no artifacts exist yet, it still prints a non-empty
    `n/a` summary instead of failing.
  - Documented the target in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` near the
    post-merge safety-net flow.
  - Added `make dev-loop-metrics` to the CLAUDE.md pre-approved
    read-only PR/Worktree command bucket because it only reads workflow
    artifacts through `gh`.
  - W5 review issues addressed during implementation: the target handles
    an empty metrics-artifact window without failing, and P50/P95 use
    nearest-rank percentiles instead of lower-rank indexing.
  - Final Step 4 verification issue addressed: the summary prints
    `runner minutes total` with lowercase `runner` so the TODO
    verification command passes as written.
work_units.summary: Add make dev-loop-metrics target for ad-hoc inspection

work_units.notes:
Before merging this PR, validate the auto-revert path end-to-end
in a fork: cherry-pick a commit that fails the post-merge tests,
push to a fork's develop, confirm the workflow opens a revert PR
with correct title/body/labels. If revert conflicts, confirm the
fallback issue is opened correctly.
Document the test in PR description AND write
`_project/decisions/dev-loop-auto-revert-fork-test-<date>.md` with
fork repo, failing SHA, workflow run URL, revert PR URL or conflict
issue URL, and screenshots/CLI excerpts sufficient for review.

Implementation record (2026-04-30):
  - A true same-account fork was impossible: GitHub rejected
    `joeharris76/BenchBox` -> `joeharris76/BenchBox-dev-loop-smoke-*`
    because one user account cannot own both a parent and a fork. No
    organization target was available, so W6 used public disposable
    mirror `joeharris76/benchbox-dev-loop-smoke-20260430`.
  - Configured the mirror and canonical repository workflow setting with
    `default_workflow_permissions=read` and
    `can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true`, which is required for
    `GITHUB_TOKEN` to create pull requests when the job requests
    `pull-requests: write`.
  - First smoke SHA `35dd478645e5ed34b5b21d33e625bab8e88ddef5`
    exposed a workflow-file edge case: GitHub rejected the revert branch
    push because the reverted commit changed `.github/workflows/*` and
    `GITHUB_TOKEN` lacks `workflows` permission.
  - W6 review issue addressed in `.github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml`:
    push failures and `gh pr create` failures now open a manual-action
    issue labeled `incident:develop-red-revert-conflict` instead of
    failing without an incident artifact.
  - Final smoke SHA `cff5c591941c989cd0c3003d552142d93489e238`
    validated the normal path: run
    `https://github.com/joeharris76/benchbox-dev-loop-smoke-20260430/actions/runs/25189439117`
    opened revert PR
    `https://github.com/joeharris76/benchbox-dev-loop-smoke-20260430/pull/1`
    from `auto-revert/cff5c591941c` to `develop` with label
    `incident:develop-red`.
  - Evidence written to
    `_project/decisions/dev-loop-auto-revert-fork-test-2026-04-30.md`.
work_units.summary: Run smoke test against a known-bad SHA in a fork
